what: Optimization initiative: 3-phase plan for DB tuning, sync compaction, and query optimization. Phase 1 decisions: split read/write connections, single JSON format kept, incremental graph expose through gateable path-by-default with auto fallback for small projects, verbose debug logs via SV_MEMORY_DEBUG env var.
why: User requested performance and memory compaction improvements. After code review, identified 10+ issues: missing PRAGMAs (cache_size, mmap_size, busy_timeout), no index on graph_edges source/target fields, N+1 queries in BFS graph traversal (mcp.go:258), leaked rows.Close() inside loop, blocking SyncFromGit on every search call, destructive full rebuild of graph, unbounded channel buffers in scanner workers, no atomic writes for memories.json.
learned: modernc.org/sqlite with WAL supports concurrent readers with 1 writer; split *sql.DB pattern is recommended over single-conn for MCP servers with mixed read/search workload. NDJSON breaks backwards compatibility for existing memories.json commits — JSON stays. Path-indexed incremental graph sync keeps performance scaling without losing correctness for small repos.
author: Mario Sandoval (Sv Tech)
impact: Clear roadmap approved by user with explicit decisions on each open question. Sets foundation for phases 2 and 3 to roll out sequentially.
next_steps: Phase 1 implementation: add PRAGMAs + connection pool split, indexes, fix rows.Close leak, mtime-based skipping of SyncFromGit in search handler. Verify with go test ./..., produce commit message, then proceed to Phase 2.
